clue.text: Bores the doctor with complaints

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
ills are ailments or complaints

explanation.surface: A tedious doctor who drones on about his patients' ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to make it with a tool that turns, as a workman's tool does.

clue.text: Men on the board getting the wind up?

explanation.surface: Chess pieces getting nervous, as if the pieces had feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Board-game discs moved on a chequered board; also currents of cold air that blow in, as 'the wind up' a chimney.

clue.text: Smoke to cause displeasure

explanation.surface: Lighting up a cigarette annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant fumes from burning gums at worship; also, to enrage or provoke someone.

clue.text: Richard the Liar? No. that's not, right!

indicators.note: not right says the preceding letters are wrongly arranged and must be put in order

explanation.surface: Someone protests at King Richard being called a liar.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'Richard the ...', so 'the' looks like part of the name, but it joins the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I of England was nicknamed Coeur de Lion, the brave-hearted king.

clue.text: Plant for a container like this

parts.note: a can is a tin or other container
thus means in this way or like this

explanation.surface: A gardener asks for a pot shaped just so for a particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean shrub with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Fish when short of ready money

definitions.text: Fish when short of ready money

parts.words: Fish when short of ready money
parts.note: a fish name is also the initials of a payment method: the full phrase is what those initials stand for, paying in ready money

explanation.definitionFit: Payment in cash made when goods arrive, abbreviated to the name of a common sea fish.

clue.text: Foster will find the railway workers quarters

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
S and E, south and east, are compass quarters

explanation.surface: A foster parent finds rail staff's lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will find' is a link; 'quarters' suggests lodgings but gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to tend and care for, as one cares for a patient.

clue.text: A man about to carry the luggage leaves

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: to carry says the word for about holds the luggage word inside it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a bag is luggage

explanation.surface: A porter is about to carry someone's bags as they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb for departing; it is the noun, the leafy parts of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is green vegetation, grass and foliage.

clue.text: What the moribund said they would do to Caesar

definitions.text: What the moribund said they would do to Caesar

parts.words: What the moribund said they would do to Caesar
parts.note: Roman gladiators about to die greeted the emperor with 'morituri te salutant'

explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators hailed the emperor before fighting, a formal greeting as soldiers give officers.

clue.text: Boxers' fight wear; these could be

definitions.note: the clue's possessive plural stands for the plural noun

indicators.note: could be says the letters before it may become something else rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on what boxers wear in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherweights are boxers in a light weight class.

clue.text: She alone has an unpleasant task with a ship

parts.note: a chore is a tedious or unpleasant job
SS, steamship, stands before a ship's name

explanation.surface: A woman left by herself to do a dreary job aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoress is a female religious recluse, a woman who lives shut away from others.

clue.text: Backing some popular urbanisation in the country

indicators.note: Backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Supporting a fashionable spread of towns into farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks LARUR out of 'popular urbanisation', and 'Backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things belonging to the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: Rifle bullet's range

parts.note: a rifle is a kind of gun
a bullet is a shot fired

explanation.surface: How far a rifle's bullet can travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunshot is the distance a gun can reach, as in 'within gunshot'.

clue.text: Arrange to carve ham

indicators.note: to arrange is to set in a new order, so the letters of the next words are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing and slicing a joint of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat to be carved; it is the verb for acting too broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated, theatrical gestures.

clue.text: The thank-you letter of a Greek

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A Greek writes a note of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Compromise to put a stop to antagonism

parts.note: to end something is to put a stop to it
anger is hostility or antagonism

explanation.surface: A peace negotiator urges concessions to halt hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise something, such as safety, is to put it at risk.

clue.text: The retiring woman's mode of dress

definitions.text: The retiring woman's mode of dress

parts.words: The retiring woman's mode of dress
parts.note: retiring reads as shy but means going to bed: what a lady wears when she turns in

explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn by women in bed.

clue.text: Normal colours

explanation.surface: Plain, ordinary shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual or typical; also a flag or banner, a regiment's colours.

clue.text: Having dug, be a pound in debt, but drier

parts.note: a dug is an udder or teat
to owe L, L being the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A gardener, having dug, is short of money but at least it's not raining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' is not the past of dig but the noun for an animal's teat; 'Having' and 'but' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea towel is the cloth used for drying washed dishes.

clue.text: Getting angrier somehow? It depends on the person

indicators.note: somehow says the word before it is reshaped in some way

explanation.surface: A remark that how angry someone gets varies with each individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is a link. 'depends' is used literally: the jewel hangs down from the wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament hanging from the lobe, so it literally hangs from someone.

clue.text: Given leave. Edward reversed the insertion

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: reversed says the name Edward's short form is written backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone granted leave, and Edward changed his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns TED into DET; 'Given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A godet is a triangular piece of cloth set into a skirt or sleeve to flare it.

clue.text: Refuse to weaken

explanation.surface: Turning down an offer weakens one's position.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer; also to deteriorate or fall away.

clue.text: Walk without hurrying — that's the way to loaf

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: Advice that the way to idle is to amble along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' reads as a verb for idling; it is the bread. 'that's' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk.

clue.text: Extremely important stations.

parts.note: read as stations at the extremities: the ones where lines finish, which are also the major ones

explanation.definitionFit: Railway stations at the ends of lines are the end points of journeys, and usually the largest.

clue.text: Fancy having left the perfect type!

parts.note: a fancy is a notion or idea

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a whim has produced the model specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a model of perfection, the best example.

clue.text: Church authority in the forefront at one hundred

indicators.note: in says the next pieces are set inside the word for the forefront

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the forefront
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A church leader stands at the head of a hundred followers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the papal government, the seat of authority of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: The girl's opposed to featuring in love-story

parts.note: love is nil, O, in tennis

indicators.note: featuring in says the letter for opposed to is placed within the word for story

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
V, versus, means against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A young woman refuses to appear in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', a link. 'love-story' looks like one thing but splits into O and LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Music-maker — a choir-man maybe

indicators.note: maybe says the letters given might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of a church choir is perhaps a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, a small instrument blown to play tunes.

clue.text: Support a heel as an upholder of the law

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
to heel over is to list, to lean to one side, of a ship

explanation.surface: A shoe repairer props up a heel, behaving like a strict official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like part of a shoe; here it is the nautical verb for leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A legalist adheres strictly to the letter of the law.

clue.text: It's fashionable to keep an eye on design

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
to tend is to look after or watch over

explanation.surface: Advice that a stylish person should watch over design.
explanation.definitionFit: To design to do something is to plan or mean to do it.
